headline: Sensex and Nifty end lower as banking and pharma drag; IT stocks rally; IDBI Bank sale approved

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: Banking, pharma, and auto sectors experienced significant selling pressure during the session
Profit booking occurred following a sharp 1,109-point rally in the previous trading session
Brokerages trimmed price targets for insurance players despite improvements in margins
Tata Technologies reported a 5% fall in net profit and contraction in margins for Q2
whatHappening: The Union Cabinet cleared the ₹52,878-crore bid by Fairfax for a majority stake in IDBI Bank
IT majors Infosys and TCS gained ground, helping to cushion the broader market decline
SEBI scheduled a SMAC meeting to review public feedback on the Consolidated Account Statement
The government approved a ₹2,009-crore bonus for over 11 lakh railway employees ahead of Diwali
summary: The Indian stock market closed lower on October 14, with the Sensex falling over 200 points amid volatile trading. While IT stocks like Infosys and TCS rallied to provide support, banking and pharma sectors faced significant selling pressure. Major corporate developments included the Cabinet's approval of the IDBI Bank sale and Tata Technologies' Q2 profit decline.
